mathematical_comparison: Both source definitions say an algebraic field extension is Galois exactly when it is separable and normal. The 9.21.1 formulation additionally notes the alternative characterization |Aut(E/F)|=[E:F], which is explicitly limited to finite extensions by Lemma 9.21.2 and cannot be silently extended to arbitrary infinite algebraic extensions.
hypotheses_for_equivalence: Algebraic extension E/F for the normal+separable characterization; finite E/F additionally for the automorphism-count equivalence.
context_specific_formulation_extra: Finite-degree automorphism count is an equivalent characterization only under the finite-extension hypothesis.
proposal: Retain both individually cited formulations as equivalent variants of one conceptual heading if cross-source grouping is later audited; list the basic separable-and-normal criterion first and the finite automorphism criterion as a conditional alternative.

mathematical_comparison: The first formulation requires every irreducible polynomial over the base having a root in K to split over K. The second requires minimal polynomials of all elements of K to split there. They are equivalent for an algebraic extension: each element's minimal polynomial is irreducible with that element a root, while any irreducible P with a root a in K is exactly a's minimal polynomial up to a nonzero scalar.
hypotheses_for_equivalence: Algebraic field extension E/F (the source definitions explicitly take this context).
context_specific_formulation_extra: Equivalent global-irreducible-polynomial and pointwise-minimal-polynomial presentations of normality.
proposal: Preserve the elementwise minimal-polynomial version and the global irreducible-polynomial version as pedagogical/equivalent source variants under a shared normal extension heading.

mathematical_comparison: Both actual Stacks source definitions require the base field to have characteristic p>0 and each element of the extension to admit a p-power lying in the base. In that context their criteria are equivalent (including exponent n=0 where appropriate). One inherited formulation additionally asserts that a trivial extension is 'purely inseparable in any characteristic'; the cited Definition 9.14.1 does not make that characteristic-zero naming convention, and the added clause must not be treated as source-supported by either citation.
hypotheses_for_equivalence: Algebraic extension of a base field with characteristic p>0, every element admits some p^n power in the base.
context_specific_formulation_extra: The characteristic-zero trivial-extension label is a possible broader convention, not verified by the two cited positive-characteristic Stacks definitions. Seek separate explicit source before retaining as a variant.
proposal: Preserve the positive-characteristic criterion as independently source-supported and flag the characteristic-zero sentence for an audited Wave 2 corrective revision or separately sourced, explicitly labeled convention. Do not mutate frozen Wave 1.

mathematical_comparison: For an algebraic extension, each element is separable if and only if its minimal polynomial is separable; the Stacks Lemma 9.12.4 characterizes such polynomials as having pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure. Thus the every-element-separable definition and the every-minimal-polynomial-has-no-repeated-root version express the same criterion.
hypotheses_for_equivalence: Algebraic field extension E/F; irreducible minimal polynomials over the base are understood.
proposal: Retain the intuitive every-element-separable formulation with the equivalent minimal-polynomial criterion as an alternate source-traceable variant.
